proof_nl:
Fix n at least 2 and a sign sequence s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Let A_s be the set of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every i=1,...,n-1. By definition, |A_s|=f(s). Similarly define A_{-s}.

Define a map T on permutations of {1,...,n} by
T(a_1,...,a_n)=(n+1-a_1,...,n+1-a_n).
Because the map x -> n+1-x is a bijection from {1,...,n} to itself, T sends permutations of {1,...,n} to permutations of {1,...,n}. Also T is an involution, since applying it twice gives back the original permutation:
T(T(a_1,...,a_n))=(a_1,...,a_n).
Hence T is a bijection on the set of all permutations of {1,...,n}.

Now take any a=(a_1,...,a_n) in A_s, and write b=T(a). For each i=1,...,n-1 we have
b_{i+1}-b_i=(n+1-a_{i+1})-(n+1-a_i)=-(a_{i+1}-a_i).
Therefore
(-s_i)(b_{i+1}-b_i)=(-s_i)(-(a_{i+1}-a_i))=s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0.
So b satisfies the defining inequalities for A_{-s}, and thus T(a) is in A_{-s}.

Conversely, if b is in A_{-s}, the same calculation applied to T(b) shows that T(b) is in A_s, because T is its own inverse. Therefore T restricts to a bijection from A_s onto A_{-s}.

Since bijective finite sets have the same cardinality, |A_s|=|A_{-s}|. Equivalently, f(s)=f(-s). This is exactly the claimed statement.
solver_summary: Use the involution T(a_1,...,a_n)=(n+1-a_1,...,n+1-a_n). It is a bijection on permutations of {1,...,n}, and it negates every adjacent difference: b_{i+1}-b_i=-(a_{i+1}-a_i). Hence a satisfies s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for all i iff T(a) satisfies (-s_i)(b_{i+1}-b_i)>0 for all i. So T gives a bijection between the permutations counted by f(s) and those counted by f(-s), proving f(s)=f(-s).
